cards.explanation: The word is fought. Joshua tells them, “…it was the LORD your God who fought for you.” (Joshua 23:3) Later he says, “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you…” (Joshua 23:10) Joshua points everyone to the LORD as the one fighting for them, so he's the one to thank.

The words are drive and possess. Joshua says the LORD their God will push those nations out of Israel's way and drive them out before them, so Israel doesn't have to do it alone. The LORD drives the nations out so Israel can take possession of their land, and Joshua says it's “…as the LORD your God promised you.” (Joshua 23:5) Driving out, taking over and a promise, all packed into one verse. That's a well-packed cookie box, friends.

The answer is to keep all that's written in the Law of Moses. Joshua says, “Be very strong, then, so that you can keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses…” (Joshua 23:6) He's talking about holding onto what God has already said. Strong here means steady, not just muscles.

The answer is False, and Joshua leaves no room for "mostly." He tells them to keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, “…not turning aside from it to the right or to the left.” (Joshua 23:6) Not a little to either side. That's the whole charge.

The answer is True. Joshua says it plainly: “You must not call on the names of their gods or swear by them, and you must not serve them or bow down to them.” (Joshua 23:7) Swearing by a god means leaning on that god's name. Joshua closes that door along with calling on the name, serving and bowing.

The answer is the LORD their God. Joshua says, “…you shall hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.” (Joshua 23:8) Notice the "…as you have done to this day." He's telling them to keep doing what they've been doing, friends.

The answer is a thousand. Joshua says, “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.” (Joshua 23:10) Look at the reason he gives: the LORD fights for them. One Israelite doesn't do this alone.

The answer is that they love the LORD their God. Joshua says, “Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.” (Joshua 23:11) After all that talk of battles and land, the thing he wants guarded is their love for the LORD.

The answer is False. Joshua says, “…the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you.” (Joshua 23:13) That's what happens if they turn away and cling to those nations. The driving out stops.

The answer is something that traps and hurts them. Joshua says those nations will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) A snare and a trap catch you, and a scourge and thorns hurt. That's four pictures in one verse, and not one of them is comfortable.

The answer is False. Joshua says, “…not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.” (Joshua 23:14) He says it two ways, back to back. He also says they know it with all their heart and soul.

The answer is True. Joshua says both halves. “…just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened…” (Joshua 23:15) I think this is a heavy verse, friends. The good promises came to pass, and Joshua says the threatened calamity will too.

The answer is breaking His covenant and serving other gods. Joshua says, “If you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you…” (Joshua 23:16) It's a serious verse. The cause is named plainly: breaking the covenant, serving other gods and bowing down to them.
